FLASHCARDS · EARLY READING

Sight word flashcards.

Learn the small words that appear on every page, one friendly picture card at a time.

What are sight words?

Sight words are the small, very common words that appear on almost every page of a children’s book: the, and, is, can, see. Many of them do not sound the way they are spelled, and many cannot be shown in a picture, so they are best learned by seeing them again and again until the child knows each one at a glance. When a child recognises these words instantly, reading stops being a slow puzzle and becomes a smooth, enjoyable story.

These 52 picture cards use words from the Dolch lists, which teachers have used for decades to build early reading. Each card shows one word in large, clear letters with a friendly picture to hold on to.

How to use the cards

Keep it short and happy: five minutes a day works better than one long session. Pick three to five new cards, read each word aloud together, and let your child point to it and say it back. Add a new card only when the old ones feel easy. If a word is hard, put it aside and bring it back tomorrow. There is no test and no rush.

Three simple games

Hide and find. Tape the cards around the room and ask your child to find the word you call out. Word hop. Lay cards on the floor like stepping stones and hop to each word while reading it. Spot it in a story. Choose a word, then look for it together on the pages of a favourite book and give a cheer every time you find one.

Sight words work best next to letter sounds and plenty of stories. If your child is still learning letters, start with the alphabet flashcards and the phonics and beginning sounds class, then share books from the Library and the storytime class.

Pre-primer words (39 cards)

The first and most useful words: short, common and easy to point at in a picture book.

Primer words (11 cards)

A step up once the first set feels easy, with colours, simple verbs and small joining words.

Grade 1 words (2 cards)

Two extra words that turn up in first stories.
